newsitem.title: USA: Pearson publishing arm sues ex-employee.
newsitem.headline: Pearson publishing arm sues ex-employee.

text.p: Penguin, Putnam Inc said on Monday that its Penguin Books USA Inc unit has filed a civil lawsuit in New Jersey District Court, alleging that a former employee conspired to defraud the company of at least $1.4 million.

According to court papers Penguin, a unit of Pearson PLC, alleged that Christina Galatro a former manager of credit and collections at its Bergenfield, N.J., office conspired with an outside collection agent, Jerome Bedell, in a scheme to divert Penguin funds for their own personal uses over a five-year period.
They "ran a racketeering scheme whereby they embezzeled funds belonging to Penguin," Penguin said in federal court papers.

Penguin said in a press release it has obtained a restitution agreement from Bedell, owner of the Parsippany, N.J., collection agency Associated Cos Inc, in which he admitted to participating with Galatro and her husband Stanley Galatro in the scheme. Bedell has agreed to repay Penguin at least $1 million, the press release said.
Penguin's press release said it uncovered the activities as part of an ongoing investigation into unauthorized discounts to certain booksellers, which it discovered earlier this year.
Pearson said in February it would take a charge against 1996 profits of 100 million sterling as a result of the unauthorized discounts, the press release said.
Bedell could not be reached at either his office or his home.
An employee at his collection agency, who declined to identify himself, said Bedell was out of the office. The employee would comment only that "I believe this has all been taken care of."
The Galatros have an unlisted home phone number and could not be contacted for comment.

In the press release, Penguin group chairman and chief executive officer Michal Lynton said, "We have compiled a compelling body of evidence that there was a deliberate conspiracy by Mrs. Galatro and an outside collection agent to embezzle over $1.4 million from Penguin."

"In the interests of our shareholders, we are seeking remedies to recover these funds, as well as other costs and damages associated with the conspiracy," Lynton's statement said. "Our investigation to date indicates that Mrs. Galatro acted without the knowledge, direction or authorization of her supervisors."

In court papers, Penguin said Galatro's and her husband's share of the scheme amounted to more than $400,000, which they used for such items as trips to Europe, Alaska and the Caribbean, as well as jewelry, theater tickets and antiques.
Galatro was a Penguin employee from 1980 until she was suspended and fired in January, the company said.
Penguin said in court papers Galatro initiated the scheme in 1992 and said it consisted of four main parts:
-- Customer debts collected by Bedell were retained by him, while Galatro deceived Penguin as to their status.
-- Galatro diverted checks to Bedell, who cashed them so as to hide the diversion.
-- Galatro concealed some of her share of the scheme's receipts by using a credit card paid for by Bedell.

-- Galatro concealed the activities from Penguin by artificially accelerating collections from customers, an effort that included unauthorized agreements to provide discounts to Penguin customers for early payment of debts, and through fraudulent and incorrect bookkeeping.
